subject: Planned: EastUS4 - Probing Window & Controlled Evacuation for Kernel Upgrade
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@brightedge.example>, BrightEdge SRE Team <sre@brightedge.example>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:00:00Z
Subject: Planned: EastUS4 - Probing Window & Controlled Evacuation for Kernel Upgrade

Hi Sam / BrightEdge SRE team,

We have a scheduled kernel maintenance in EastUS4 next week that requires a short probing window followed by controlled host evacuations for a kernel/driver upgrade. This note explains the plan, expected impact, and mitigation steps so you can prepare long-running jobs or pinned instances.

Summary
- What: Kernel version bump + driver alignment (runtime hotpatch path)
- Where: EastUS4, affected host pools serving your pinned capacity and shared pools
- When: 2026-12-22 02:00 UTC start (probing), 2026-12-22 03:00–06:00 UTC controlled evacuations in waves
- Expected customer-visible impact: brief TCP connection resets for in-flight requests during an individual host evacuation (typical recovery <90s). No mass region outage expected.

How we'll run it (high level)
1) 02:00 UTC: probing window on a small canary subset to validate KV-cache warmup and quantized kernel behavior.
2) 03:00 UTC onwards: sequenced evacuations in 15–30 minute waves with health gates.
3) We will automatically route traffic off a draining host, with pass-through fallback to reserve capacity.

What we recommend for BrightEdge
- Avoid starting new long-running model exports between 01:30–07:00 UTC on 2026-12-22.
- If you rely on pinned capacity, please ensure your pinning is up-to-date in the console; we will coordinate pinned-host exceptions where necessary.

Attachments: runbook and customer-facing evacuation checklist attached.

If this window conflicts with a critical workflow for you, reply with the specific job IDs or times and we will escalate to schedule exceptions.

Thanks,

--
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: eastus4-probing-runbook.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: evacuation-checklist.csv (text/csv)]

From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@brightedge.example>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
Cc: BrightEdge SRE Team <sre@brightedge.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-20T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Planned: EastUS4 - Probing Window & Controlled Evacuation for Kernel Upgrade

Thanks Olga — appreciate the heads up. A couple quick questions:

1) We run daily heavy batch exports that start at 02:15 UTC and usually take ~2.5 hours. Will those jobs be retried automatically by your client when a host reset occurs?
2) Can you confirm which host pools our "brightedge-pinned-1" pin is on so we can validate failover windows on our side?

If the batch runs will see more than transient retries, we may need you to either shift our pinned hosts out of the rotation or move the maintenance start by a few hours.

Best,
Sam
Senior SRE, BrightEdge Media

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@brightedge.example>, BrightEdge SRE Team <sre@brightedge.example>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Planned: EastUS4 - Probing Window & Controlled Evacuation for Kernel Upgrade

Hi Sam — quick answers below and next steps.

1) Client retries: the Redwood SDK will automatically surface transient network errors as retries for standard generation calls, but long-running export jobs that maintain a persistent socket may see a short interruption. For most customers we detect evacuation and surface a retryable 5xx for in-flight requests; our ingestion service layer will re-queue generation chunks. We cannot guarantee client-side logic outside our SDK.

2) Pinned hosts: brightedge-pinned-1 is on pool euclid-3 (EastUS4). I can request a temporary pin-exclusion for your account for this window if you prefer — that would keep your hosts out of the evacuation waves. Note that pin-exclusion reduces available capacity headroom for others and may increase queueing if demand spikes.

Mitigation options we can offer now
- Option A: Temporary pin-exclusion for brightedge-pinned-1 for 2026-12-22 01:30–07:30 UTC (we will need an explicit approval from your team).
- Option B: Shift evacuation window to start at 07:00 UTC (we can accommodate if notified by 2026-12-21 12:00 UTC).
- Option C: Keep window as-is and rely on automatic routing + SDK retries; we will increase capacity in adjacent pools to reduce queueing risk.

Next steps
- If you want Option A, reply with approval and we will apply the exclusion and send a confirmation.
- If you need Option B, let us know the decision by EOD 2026-12-21.

I'll also add a short runbook excerpt to the JIRA ticket (JIRA-OPS-2871) for your SREs to review.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evacuation-checklist.csv (text/csv)]

From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@brightedge.example>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.example>
Cc: BrightEdge SRE Team <sre@brightedge.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-12-21T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Planned: EastUS4 - Probing Window & Controlled Evacuation for Kernel Upgrade

Thanks Marcus — Option A works for us. Please proceed with the temporary pin-exclusion for brightedge-pinned-1 for the window you outlined. We approve the exclusion and will hold batch starts until 07:30 UTC as a precaution.

For your post-event follow-up can you also include a short list of any requests we should run (log exports, trace IDs) so we can coordinate a targeted postmortem?

Appreciate the quick responses.

Best,
Sam
Senior SRE, BrightEdge Media
